newsitem.title: UK: London gold steady after bounce late on Friday.
newsitem.headline: London gold steady after bounce late on Friday.

text.p: Gold held steady on Monday after a late bounce on Friday, but trade was lackadaisical due to the Labor Day holiday in the United States.
Bullion closed at $386.90 per ounce, up 55 cents from Friday's London finish.
Dealers and analysts are looking for this week to be key to the market, with charts giving mixed signals and the slow summer season coming to a close.
"Tomorrow will be very important since technically both gold and silver are at a crossroads and also all the big fund managers will be returning," one dealer said.
Another dealer said the market was also eyeing rallying oil prices, since investors could look to gold as a hedge against inflation.
The market bounced late on Friday, mainly led by strength in silver, after slipping, dealers said.
"Silver led the precious complex higher on short covering late on Friday, which was in turn due to the rally in copper," one dealer said.
Silver, unlike gold, has mainly industrial uses, so market sentiment got a shot in the arm when the flagship industrial metal copper roared higher on Friday, breaking out of its range.
The gold market rallied from its recent low of $380 hit in early July but failed to penetrate the next significant barrier at $390 and has been hovering under it since.
Another brief surge in copper on Monday morning failed to translate into fresh gains for any of the precious metals.
Silver held at last week's firmer levels, ending the day at $5.19 per ounce, up three cents from Friday's London close.
Platinum and palladium were less affected, with platinum slightly higher at $396.00 per ounce, up around 60 cents, and palladium 50 cents firmer at $126.00.
